The operational restriction on gpt-oss-120b is that it **must not be run unattended** until the cause of a decode hang is understood.

The reason given is that **the first time gpt-oss-120b was loaded, it hung and produced nothing**, and this failure has not been reproduced or diagnosed. Although it has behaved correctly on every subsequent load (more than a dozen), the unexplained hang remains a risk, and the model is not to be left running unattended until this issue is resolved.
records.peer_answer:
**Restriction** – When gpt‑oss‑120b (≈ 60 GiB‑plus weights) is being loaded you must **not run any heavy disk‑I/O at the same time and you must be present to power‑cycle the machine if the load stalls**.  

**Why** – The dead‑lock fingerprint (see *memory‑edge‑deadlock.md*) shows that loading a near‑edge model while the system is under memory pressure (total RAM usage > 128 GB, most easily caused by concurrent large file‑hashes, downloads, backups, etc.) starves the amdgpu driver’s small‑buffer suballocator. The wedged process becomes an uninterruptible D‑state task (`drm_suballoc_new`) that **SIGKILL cannot kill and a graceful `sudo reboot` stalls**; the only way to recover is a **hard physical power‑cycle**. Therefore the operational rule is to avoid concurrent heavy I/O during the load and to have an operator (Alastair) physically present to power‑cycle if the load ever hangs.
